statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 venues are inside the CME weekend halt, with Tail low and Stress high.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold. CME equity futures are halted until Sunday 22:00Z, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop anywhere in this horizon. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a record close through the weekend halt: Friday's completed retracement and a 15.31 VIX keep Tail low, while Brent near $102.70 and a 5.28% 10-year keep Stress high
body: Friday 2 October closed the Nasdaq-100 at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00%, but the close sat 209.60 points below the 31,017.53 session high and only 70.86 above the 30,737.07 low, so the session ended with its retracement completed rather than holding an extreme. That distinction matters more than the record itself: extreme-holding is a Tail amplifier, a completed give-back is not. VIX fell 6.59% to 15.31 and settled at the bottom of its 15.30-16.24 range, so realised volatility decayed into the close. September payrolls arrived at 29,000 against roughly 90,000 expected, with unemployment up to 4.2% and average hourly earnings at 0.1% month-on-month, cutting October rate-hike odds to about 16-20% from near 64% a week earlier while the funds target stayed at 3.75-4.00%. Rates nonetheless round-tripped and firmed: the 10-year traded as low as 5.18% immediately after the print before closing up about 4 basis points at 5.283%, and the 30-year dipped to 5.57% before finishing at 5.63%. Equities at a record against a firmer long end is a cross-asset conflict, which raises Stress and tempers conviction rather than raising Tail, and the round trip itself is evidence of orderly two-way discovery. Leadership was narrow: Nvidia set a record near $237.75, up about 2.9% alongside a $150bn buyback addition, while Micron fell 1.50% and Seagate and Western Digital each lost more than 12%, and the Nasdaq Composite's 1.2% gain to 27,190.86 was the only weekly advance among the major indices. Energy remains the dominant Stress input and cuts both ways: the G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels over four months through the IEA, roughly 830,000 barrels a day with substantial diesel inside the first 20 days, and WTI fell 1.90% to $91.11 after touching a one-month low of $88.06, yet Brent closed effectively flat at $102.25 and was quoted near $102.70 at 04:25Z, the Strait of Hormuz remained insurance-closed on day 216 with 139 AIS-visible vessels holding away from berth, UKMTO reported a fifth recent tanker strike on Friday, and reporting points to a third U.S. carrier strike group moving to the region. None of that has been expressed in a tradeable Nasdaq-100 book, because CME equity futures halted on Friday at 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, which is beyond this horizon. With no price path available to fail, Tail is held at 8 and the mapped state is green, while Stress stays at 65 on the energy and term-premium pair and Confidence is 85 on directly verified levels, yields, crude, volatility and calendar evidence, trimmed slightly because the shared Finviz context is four days stale and partial and because live intraday structure is structurally unavailable during a halt.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover Friday's U.S. session and the first seven hours of the weekend halt. Published Claude history shows Tail peaking in an orange 25-27 band across the 13:00-14:00Z cash-open hours, easing to a yellow 21-23 through the afternoon, then falling to green single digits from 21:00Z as the cash close completed its retracement and CME futures entered the weekend halt. Stress held in the high 65-79 band throughout on the energy and long-end backdrop, and Confidence ranged between 82 and 89.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which began Friday at 21:00Z and runs until the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop and Tail stays low and flat at 8 before nudging to 9 in the back half purely on accumulating unpriced weekend headline risk. The mapped state is green throughout. Stress eases from 65 to about 62 through the dead Saturday hours, then firms to 67 by the end of the window as the closed strait, the incomplete G7 release and a 5.28% 10-year are all carried forward unpriced. Confidence decays from 85 to 75 purely as Friday's verified evidence ages. Both genuine checkpoints lie beyond this window: Monday's ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z, consensus near 55.1 against 55.4 prior, and Wednesday's FOMC Minutes at 18:00Z. Any weekend escalation or G7 implementation news could only be priced at the reopen, which is also outside this horizon.

Stress stays high because equities set a record while the long end firmed: the 10-year closed up about 4bp at 5.28% and the 30-year at 5.63%, a cross-asset conflict rather than an aligned trend.

The labour print behind Friday's move is soft: 29,000 September payrolls against roughly 90,000 expected, unemployment up to 4.2% and average hourly earnings at 0.1% month-on-month. That cooled October rate-hike odds to about 16-20% from near 64% a week earlier.

A notable Tail-negative detail from Friday is that the rates move also round-tripped: the 10-year traded as low as 5.18% straight after the payroll print before closing back at 5.28%. Orderly two-way price discovery is the opposite of a no-retracement path.

30-year dipped to 5.57% intraday before closing at 5.63%
Two-way discovery in rates argues against mean-reversion failure

Crude direction is conflicting, not aligned.

WTI -1.90% to $91.11 after a one-month low of $88.06
Conflicting crude direction lowers directional conviction

forecast.analysis: The halt holds through the European Saturday. The supply-relief leg of the energy story is the G7 agreement to release up to 100 million barrels over four months through the IEA, about 830,000 barrels a day, with substantial diesel in the first 20 days. Crude releases do not convert directly into diesel.

Roughly 830,000 b/d if spread evenly; diesel first in 20 days
Refinery capacity limits how fast crude becomes diesel
Supply relief offsets escalation risk: a Stress input both ways
